title: Sirens, Smiles and a Serious Message: LISD Kicks Off Safe Schools and School Bus Safety Week With Multi-Agency Parade
excerpt: LISD opened America's Safe Schools Week and National School Bus Safety Week on Oct. 20 with a proclamation at the Performing Arts Complex and a lights-and-sirens parade of LISD Police, Webb County Sheriff's and Constable's offices, Laredo PD, and DPS vehicles past 20 campuses.
content:
Laredo students got a loud, cheerful reminder on Monday, Oct. 20, that safety is a team effort, as the Laredo Independent School District kicked off America's Safe Schools Week and National School Bus Safety Week with a proclamation ceremony and a multi-agency parade, according to LISD.

The morning began at the LISD Performing Arts Complex, where Board of Trustees Vice President Rodolfo "Rudy" Morales, III, Trustee Monica Garcia, and Superintendent of Schools Dr. Sylvia G. Rios read the official proclamation. Martin High School student Belen Loredo performed the National Anthem, and Leyendecker Elementary School students Valeria Aguilar, Ryder Sanchez, Scott Aguilar, and Lunah Hernandez led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Then came the main event. Patrol units and emergency vehicles from the LISD Police Department, the Webb County Constable's Office, the Webb County Sheriff's Office, the Laredo Police Department, the Texas Department of Public Safety, and other agencies assembled at Garden Avenue and San Bernardo Avenue before setting off from Martin High School in a red, white, and blue show of lights and sirens. Martin High School cheerleaders and Tigerettes and the Christen Middle School band waved the convoy on, and the parade rolled past 20 LISD campuses, where students lined fences and sidewalks to watch — among them the youngsters at Leon Daiches Elementary School, who took in the passing police cars and fire trucks from their campus.

The LISD Police Department and the district's Health and Occupational Safety Support Services Department organized the celebration. Executive Director Dr. Oscar Perez told the crowd that safety is a shared responsibility for students, staff, and the community, and that the district works to build a safety culture so students know they are protected at all times.

Transportation Department Director Alexis Solis used the occasion to remind drivers to keep their distance from school buses — as he put it, "stand back from the yellow and black" — and asked the community to thank bus drivers, bus monitors, mechanics, and transportation staff for the work they do every day.

LISD Police Chief Doreen Hale also marked the week by thanking the district's partners and staff, saying the collective effort to keep schools safe havens for learning requires continuing collaboration among law enforcement, educators, parents, and students, including proactively identifying potential threats.

America's Safe Schools Week was established in 1984 by the National School Safety Center and is observed each October alongside National School Bus Safety Week. Both observances highlight keeping campuses free of crime and violence and getting students to and from school safely — a mission Laredo's agencies showed up for in force this week.

Sources: Laredo Independent School District (laredoisd.org), "LISD celebrates America's Safe Schools and National School Bus Safety Week" (Oct. 2026); Leon Daiches Elementary School campus post (Oct. 20, 2026).

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, News Anchors, Webb Watch 956
